title: PHP semantics a fine-print port must reproduce

contract.summary: The PHP behaviours under the writer that no platform library reproduces: %.4F's tie rule, round()'s pre-rounding, number_format, and mbstring's '?' substitution. A port implements each in a php helper module and runs these rows against it.

functions.num: num(value) -> string -- Syntax::num: sprintf('%.4F') trimmed, no exponent, no negative zero
functions.rgb: rgb(hex) -> [r, g, b] -- Syntax::rgb: round(channel / 255, 4); [0, 0, 0] for anything but #RRGGBB
functions.numberFormat: numberFormat(value, decimals) -> string -- number_format with '.' and ','
functions.text: text(utf8Base64) -> string -- Syntax::text: hex UTF-16BE with a BOM; C0 controls except tab and LF dropped
functions.name: name(bytesBase64) -> string -- Syntax::name: #xx outside the regular characters
functions.validUtf8: validUtf8(bytesBase64) -> base64 -- mb_convert_encoding UTF-8 to UTF-8 substitution
functions.winAnsi: winAnsi(text) -> lowercase hex -- StandardFont::encode: WinAnsiEncoding by table, FOLD, then '?'

contract.referenceNote: Run on PHP 8.4 by the exporter; SPEC section 4.1 records the tie rules measured.

notes: Rows are EXPORTED from PHP by fine-print/tests/Conformance/Export.php (composer conformance:export) and are never edited by hand or regenerated by a port. fine-print's DriftTest re-exports to a temporary directory and fails if anything here moved.

No discrimination probe for the writer itself lives here: the implementation under test is a PDF writer, which this package does not carry (the same known gap as flow/graph-runs). canon() IS small enough to carry: tests/fine-print-canon.test.ts re-implements it independently of the exporter, checks it against every writer-bytes artifact, and pins its mutants.
